newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's meetings to be limited this week.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's meetings to be limited this week.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will concentrate on preparing his annual report to parliament at a residence outside Moscow this week and meetings will be limited, the Kremlin said on Monday.

Yeltsin, recovering from pneumonia, has visited the Kremlin only three times since he went down with the illness on January 8, just two weeks after he returned to his office after a heart operation in November.

"All the head of state's aides will take an active part in the work on the document in the Gorky-9 residence. In connection with this the number of the president's meetings will be limited," Interfax news agency said, quoting spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky.
"This, however, does not concern Boris Yeltsin's traditional Tuesday meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin," Yastrzhembsky said.
A Kremlin press spokesman confirmed the report and said a meeting with Chernomyrdin "could not be excluded".
Yeltsin held talks with visiting French President Jacques Chirac on Sunday, his first meeting with a Western leader since the pneumonia struck.
Chirac told reporters he had held more than three hours of talks with the Kremlin leader, and was very impressed with the speed of Yeltsin's recovery.
Yeltsin had multiple bypass surgery on November 5 and has appeared rarely in the Kremlin since he was re-elected in July.
